nodes.summary: Write $F_j$ for the $j$-th Fibonacci number. For every natural number $n \ge 7$ with $n \ne 12$, $F_n$ has a primitive divisor with respect to the discriminant $5$: there is a prime $p$ that divides $F_n$ but does not divide $5 F_1 F_2 \cdots F_{n-1}$.
nodes.title: Primitive divisors of Fibonacci numbers

nodes.summary: Let $u_0, u_1, u_2, \dots$ be a sequence of integers and let $D$ be an integer (for a Lucas pair $(\alpha, \beta)$, the discriminant $D = (\alpha - \beta)^2$). A natural number $p$ is a primitive divisor of $u_n$ when $n \ge 1$, $p$ is prime, $p$ divides $u_n$, and $p$ does not divide $D \, u_1 u_2 \cdots u_{n-1}$ (for $n = 1$ the product is empty, and the condition is that $p$ does not divide $D$).
nodes.title: Primitive divisor relative to a discriminant

nodes.summary: Let $(a_s)_{s \ge 0}$ be a sequence of integers and let $m$ and $u$ be natural numbers. Then $u$ is a primitive divisor of $a_m$ when $m \ge 1$, $u \ge 2$, $u$ divides $a_m$, and $u$ divides no $a_s$ with $1 \le s < m$.
nodes.title: Primitive divisor of an integer sequence

nodes.summary: Let $(a_s)_{s \ge 0}$ be a sequence of integers and let $m$ and $u$ be natural numbers. Then $u$ is a primitive prime divisor of $a_m$ when $u$ is prime and $u$ is a primitive divisor of $a_m$.
nodes.title: Primitive prime divisor of an integer sequence

nodes.summary: Let $(a_s)_{s \ge 0}$ be a sequence of integers and let the natural number $u$ be a primitive divisor of $a_m$. If $n \ge 1$ and $u$ divides $a_n$, then $m \le n$.
nodes.title: A primitive divisor appears at the least positive index

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be integers with $Q \ne 0$, and let $(u_n)_{n \ge 0}$ be the integer sequence with $u_0 = 0$, $u_1 = 1$ and $u_{n+2} = Pu_{n+1} - Qu_n$ (the Lucas sequence of the first kind). Suppose the sequence is nondegenerate: whenever complex numbers $\alpha$ and $\beta$ satisfy $\alpha + \beta = P$, $\alpha\beta = Q$ and $\beta \ne 0$, no power $(\alpha / \beta)^k$ with $k \ge 1$ equals $1$. nodes.title: Somer's primitive divisor theorem

nodes.summary: Let $(a_s)_{s \ge 0}$ be a sequence of integers. If a natural number $u$ is a primitive prime divisor of both $a_m$ and $a_n$, then $m = n$.
nodes.title: A primitive prime divisor occurs at only one index

nodes.summary: Let $(a_s)_{s \ge 0}$ be a sequence of integers. If a natural number $u$ is a primitive divisor of both $a_m$ and $a_n$, then $m = n$.
nodes.title: A primitive divisor occurs at only one index

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
